best_for: People who still own classic point-and-click adventures on discs or from GOG and Steam and want them to run on a modern PC, Mac or Linux box.
description:
ScummVM is a program from the ScummVM Team that runs classic point-and-click adventures and role-playing games on computers they were never made for. The name stands for Script Creation Utility for Maniac Mansion Virtual Machine.

It supports more than 325 adventure games from studios such as LucasArts, Sierra On-Line, Revolution Software, Cyan and Westwood, so you can go back to Monkey Island, Broken Sword, Myst or Blade Runner, or dig up obscure titles you missed. New games open for public testing in the daily builds. One example is Pendulo Studios' 1997 comedy Hollywood Monsters, which was sold only in Spanish and Italian and now comes with English subtitles in ScummVM.

points.title: Bring your own games
points.text: ScummVM ships no commercial games. It replaces the original game program, so you need the data files from a copy you own. The project refuses to support pirated copies and warns they can carry malware.

points.title: Some games are free
points.text: The site has a section of freeware games and demos, so you can try it before digging out old discs.

points.title: Not an emulator
points.text: It reimplements each game's engine instead of emulating old hardware. The 2026.4.0 release in October 2026 added 194 games across 12 new engines.

points.title: Check the compatibility list
points.text: Not every game runs on every platform, and only some games can load saves from the original release. The Compatibility page lists the state of each title.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: ScummVM is GPL software with no price. It also runs on Android, iOS, Switch and many older systems.

points.title: Linux: the verified Flatpak
points.text: The Flathub build is published by the ScummVM Team and verified. The project also offers .deb packages for Debian and Ubuntu and a Snap.

points.title: Older systems still covered
points.text: The universal Mac build needs macOS 10.13; separate builds go back to OS X 10.4 on PowerPC. On Windows this page lists one installer for all users and keeps 14 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
